Oak Bluffs.metaDescription: Bats, raccoons, and skunks removed in Oak Bluffs, MA — Campground cottages to Lagoon Pond. Island homes served by our crew, same-day when ferries allow. Call us.
Oak Bluffs.housing_era: Oak Bluffs is famous for its colorful Victorian gingerbread cottages in the Campground, plus Victorian and early-1900s homes around Ocean Park, cottage neighborhoods toward the Lagoon, and many seasonal houses that close for winter.
Oak Bluffs.geographic_features: Oak Bluffs Harbor (ferry and boating harbor), Lagoon Pond (large pond shared with Tisbury), Martha's Vineyard Sound (water along the north shore), Ocean Park (open green facing the sound)

Oak Bluffs.wildlife_intro:
Oak Bluffs packs a lot of housing into a small, very seasonal town, and wildlife takes full advantage. The Campground's gingerbread cottages, with their ornate trim, layered roofs, and long winter closures, are prime bat and squirrel housing — colonies settle in while streets sit empty. Raccoons work chimneys and trash around Ocean Park and Eastville, skunks den under cottage porches, and white-footed mice move into closed homes around Lagoon Pond every fall.

Our island work in Oak Bluffs follows the ferry-season rhythm. Spring openings bring the discoveries: bat colonies in cottage attics, squirrel nests in eaves, mouse damage in kitchens. Summer brings raccoon families and skunk calls from occupied homes. Our crew plans island trips carefully, brings everything needed to inspect, remove, and seal in one visit, and works as a MassWildlife-licensed Problem Animal Control agent — bats by exclusion only, in the permitted May and August-to-October windows. Call us early in the season for the fastest scheduling.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Oak Bluffs?
faqs.a: Island jobs depend on the animal, the cottage, and how much sealing is needed — the Campground's detailed Victorian trim often means more entry points to close. We inspect, explain the work, and quote the complete job before starting. Call us to coordinate an inspection around your opening dates.

faqs.q: Why are bats such a problem in Campground cottages?
faqs.a: The cottages were built as summer homes: thin walls, decorative roof trim, and months of quiet emptiness each winter are exactly what a bat colony wants. Small gaps at eaves and gables let bats in, and colonies return to the same cottage each year. Our crew seals those gaps after a permitted exclusion, which is the only way to keep a cottage bat-free for good.

Edgartown.wildlife_intro:

Bats roost in the attics of whaling captains' houses downtown, where old chimneys and complex rooflines offer plenty of gaps. Raccoons and skunks work the Katama neighborhoods and farm edges, gray squirrels move through the oak streets, and on Chappaquiddick, raccoons, skunks, and mice are the steady issues in scattered homes surrounded by refuge land and scrub.

Most Edgartown calls come at the shoulders of the season. Spring openings uncover bat colonies and overwintering rodents in houses closed since fall; late summer brings raccoon and skunk problems in occupied homes. Our crew coordinates island scheduling so inspection, removal, and sealing happen in as few trips as possible, and all work follows Massachusetts PAC rules — bats excluded only in the May and August-to-October windows, and no wildlife moved off a property, since state law prohibits it. Call us to plan work around your season.

faqs.q: What does wildlife removal cost in Edgartown?

We inspect the home, explain the scope in full, and quote the price before starting. Call us to arrange an inspection, especially ahead of spring opening.

Yes — our crew crosses on the Chappy ferry and services homes across Chappaquiddick. Calls there are usually raccoons, skunks, bats in seasonal homes, and mice over the winter. Because the trip takes planning, call us as early as you can and we will group the inspection and work efficiently.

Tisbury.wildlife_intro:
Tisbury is Vineyard Haven — the island's working port and its most year-round community — so wildlife calls here never fully stop. Raccoons den in chimneys and attics around the harbor village, bats roost in older homes near Main Street and in West Chop summer houses, and skunks and opossums work yards across town. Around Lake Tashmoo and Lambert's Cove, raccoons, squirrels, and white-footed mice are the regulars, and rats appear near the ferry and restaurant blocks.

The seasonal swing is still real: West Chop and other summer homes opened in spring reveal bat colonies and mouse damage from the closed months, and our crew seals those houses before the season starts. Year-round homes keep us busy with raccoon families in spring, skunk dens in summer, and rodent exclusion in fall. All work is done as a MassWildlife-licensed Problem Animal Control agent, with bat exclusion in the permitted windows only. Call us — we schedule island work promptly, same day when the boats and the job allow.

West Tisbury.wildlife_intro:
West Tisbury feels like farm country, and its wildlife calls match: raccoons in farmhouse chimneys and barn-adjacent attics, bats in the eaves of older homes along Music Street and the town center, and skunks under porches from North Tisbury to Lambert's Cove. Gray squirrels and white-footed mice are constant in houses backed by oak woods, and properties near Tisbury Great Pond and Mill Brook see raccoon and skunk traffic following the water.

Many West Tisbury homes are seasonal or visited in stretches, so our crew often opens a job at a house that has sat quiet — bats in the attic, mice in the walls, a raccoon that raised young in the chimney. We clear the animals, seal the entry points, and leave the house secure until the next visit. Work follows Massachusetts PAC rules, including exclusion-only bat removal in the permitted May and August-to-October windows. Call us to schedule island service; planning ahead helps us combine the trip with the work in a single visit.

faqs.q: What does wildlife removal cost in West Tisbury?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the animal, the house, and how much exclusion work is needed — older farmhouses often have several gaps to seal. We inspect first, explain everything we find, and quote the complete job before starting. Call us to arrange an inspection at your West Tisbury property.

faqs.q: Something raised young in our chimney while we were away. What was it?
faqs.a: Most often a raccoon — uncapped chimneys are favorite den sites, and a quiet seasonal house is ideal. Our crew checks whether the family is still present, and if the young are mobile, uses exclusion so the family leaves together, then caps and seals the chimney. Massachusetts law does not allow moving wildlife off the property, so keeping them out permanently is the real solution.

Chilmark.geographic_features: Menemsha Harbor (working fishing harbor and village), Menemsha Pond (pond behind the harbor), Chilmark Pond (south-shore coastal pond), Squibnocket (headland and beach area in the southwest)

Chilmark.wildlife_intro:
Chilmark's stone walls, farms, and empty winter roads make it prime wildlife country. Raccoons are the top call — in chimneys, barns, and attics along Middle Road — followed by skunks under porches in Menemsha and around Beetlebung Corner, and bats in the attics of older and seasonal homes. Gray squirrels and white-footed mice move into houses backed by oak woods, and the harbor village sees raccoon activity around fishing gear, bait, and trash through the season.

Because so many Chilmark homes sit empty for long stretches, discoveries usually happen at opening: droppings in the attic, a skunk den under the porch, mice through the kitchen. Our crew plans up-island trips to handle inspection, removal, and sealing together, so a house is secure by the time we leave. All work is done under Massachusetts PAC rules — bats by exclusion only in the permitted windows, and no off-property moving of wildlife. Call us before opening season for the smoothest scheduling.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Chilmark?
faqs.a: Pricing depends on the species, the property, and the amount of sealing the house needs, which we determine at inspection. Rural homes often have outbuildings and multiple gaps to account for. We explain the full scope and quote the job before any work begins — call us to plan a visit.

faqs.q: Raccoons keep getting into things around Menemsha harbor. What helps most?
faqs.a: Securing the attractants: tight-lidded trash containers, no bait or fish scraps left accessible, and pet food brought indoors. For raccoons already denning in a chimney or attic, our crew uses exclusion so they leave, then caps and seals the opening. With harbor food sources nearby, sealing the building is what keeps new raccoons from moving in.

Skunks den under porches and sheds, raccoons work chimneys and trash along Moshup Trail and in Lobsterville, and bats roost in the attics of seasonal homes that sit closed through the winter. White-footed mice are a constant in houses at the woods' edge, and squirrels get into eaves where oaks overhang the roof.

Our crew treats Aquinnah work with the planning an up-island trip deserves: call ahead, and we arrive ready to inspect, remove, and seal in one visit. Spring openings at seasonal homes are the most common job — clearing bats, mice, or a raccoon family and closing the gaps before summer. Everything follows Massachusetts PAC rules, with bat exclusion only in the permitted May and August-to-October windows. Call us and we will coordinate timing with you; for a small town at the end of the island, early booking makes all the difference.

faqs.q: What does wildlife removal cost in Aquinnah?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the animal involved, the home, and how much sealing and cleanup the job requires. We inspect the property, explain what we found, and quote the complete job before starting any work. Call us to schedule — up-island visits are planned in advance so the trip covers everything.

faqs.q: Do you work respectfully around tribal and conservation land in Aquinnah?

The cliffs and surrounding habitat support protected wildlife; our job is limited to animals inside or under your home, handled legally and humanely.
